newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans drop on commodity fund sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans drop on commodity fund sales.

text.p: Heavy commodity fund selling sparked sharp losses in July soybeans at midsession Wednesday, floor traders said.
"The funds hit the beans on the open after we had spent all morning talking about how much higher we were going to be," said one floor trader.
Traders had initially called the soybean market to open two to five cents per bushel higher, but July opened down instead.
Near the open, Refco sold 6.0 million bushels July and 2.5 million November, and Lind Waldock sold three million bushels July, pit sources said.

New crop contracts were also under pressure from weather considered ideal for growth and development. Temperatures have warmed significantly in much of the Midwest, which is speeding the crop development, traders said.
Some traders said they expected speculators to continue to exit July positions as the market trades erratically.
"Specs (speculative traders) like long-term trending markets," said one trader.
At 1122 CDT, July soybeans were down sixteen cents per bushel at $8.37 and other months were 1/2 to nine cents lower.
